title: Talent acquisition and first-120-days handbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This handbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard hiring workflow, interviewer calibration guidance, candidate SLAs, offer/negotiation guardrails, and the structured first-120-days (manager + new-hire) ramp plan. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, and people-ops partners.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce variability in hiring outcomes, accelerate new-hire productivity, and provide managers pragmatic checklists to own execution.
- Scope: All full-time and core contractor hires across engineering, product, and go-to-market teams. Excludes contingent vendors and agency contractors (see vendor onboarding doc).

Principles we follow
1) Candidate experience matters: respond within SLA windows, transparent feedback, respectful scheduling.
2) Evidence-based hiring: decisions rely on rubric scores + hiring manager calibration.
3) Manager ownership: hiring, onboarding logistics, and performance signals are manager responsibilities with people-ops support.
4) Continuous calibration: interviewers attend quarterly calibration sessions and update rubrics.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference)
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview panel selection, final decision, first-120-days plan, career conversation at 90/120 days.
- Recruiter: sourcing strategy, scheduling, offer preparation, candidate communications, diversity sourcing targets.
- Interviewers: complete rubrics, provide written feedback within 48 hours, surface concerns early.
- People Ops: compensation bands, background checks, documentation, onboarding logistics, run manager calibration training.

Standard hiring workflow (timeline expectations)
1) Role kickoff (Day 0–3)
   - Manager completes role brief template (template link) and must attach: job mission, top 3 success metrics for first 6 months, required vs nice-to-have skills, proposed interview loop.
2) Sourcing and sieve (Day 1–14)
   - Recruiter returns shortlist within 7–10 business days for active reqs. Diversity-sourcing target: at least 30% of longlist from underrepresented groups where feasible.
3) Interview loop (Day 7–21)
   - Interview panel: 4–6 interviews (technical, design, system sense, collaboration/culture) recommended. No more than 2 back-to-back interviews without a 15-minute break.
4) Decision and offer (Day 21–28)
   - Hiring manager submits hire memo with anonymized rubric summary. Recruiter prepares offer within 48 hours of approval.
5) Acceptance to start (Day 30–60)
   - Standard notice period target: 30 days. Escalate if longer to people-ops for special onboarding support.

Candidate experience SLA (service-level agreements)
- Recruiter initial reply to inbound application: 2 business days.
- First interview scheduled after initial screen: within 7 business days for active roles.
- Interview feedback provided to candidate: within 7 business days of final interview.
- Offer response window: standard 7 calendar days (extendable with recruiter approval).

Interview rubric (scoring and guidance)
- Scoring scale: 1–5 (1 = does not meet, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = outstanding).
- Dimensions (apply per role):
  - Core competency (domain knowledge / technical skill)
  - Problem solving & debugging
  - System design / architecture (if applicable)
  - Collaboration & communication
  - Ownership & execution
  - Role-specific signals (product sense, sales aptitude, security mindshare)
- Minimum hire thresholds (guideline): average score >= 3.5 AND no single dimension < 2 unless hiring manager documents a compelling exception.

Example rubric table (paste into interview form)
| Dimension | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Problem solving | Incorrect approach, cannot reason about tradeoffs | Basic solution with gaps | Solid approach, some clarity issues | Strong approach with good tradeoffs | Exceptional insight and tradeoff analysis |
| Collaboration | Unable to accept feedback | Limited examples of teamwork | Clear examples of cross-team work | Drives collaboration proactively | Influences cross-org outcomes |

Calibration & training
- Quarterly calibration sessions run by people-ops (60 minutes). Attendance required for interviewers who did >6 interviews that quarter.
- Calibration agenda: 3 anonymized debriefs, rubric edge cases, signal alignment for leveling.

Offer & comp guidelines
- Compensation anchors: use current comp bands (see related_pages). Compensation must be approved by people-ops for any offer above band midpoint + 15%.
- Equity: recommended grants for ICs and managers based on level (see comp bands doc).
- Counter-offer handling: recruiter and manager coordinate; avoid incentivizing multiple-stage counter cycles.

Background checks & compliance
- Standard pre-hire checks: identity verification, employment verification, and reference check for ICs at level 4+.
- For hires in regulated markets (EU data residency or healthcare customers): initiate enhanced checks (people-ops will advise).

First-120-days structured ramp (manager + new-hire checklists)
Manager checklist (pre-boarding) — 2 weeks before start:
- Confirm offer acceptance and start date in HRIS.
- Add to team calendar, assign buddy, confirm hardware & network access, create agenda for day 1.

Day 1–14: orientation & context
- Week 1 objectives:
  - Orientation: company mission, code of conduct, security basics (complete security course by day 5).
  - Team orientation: context doc, architecture tour, current roadmap, key stakeholders.
  - Quick win: assign a read-only task and a small actionable task to deliver in week 2.
- Manager deliverables: 30-minute daily check-ins for week 1, assign a mentor, set expectations for 1:1 cadence.

Day 15–60: ownership & delivery
- Objectives:
  - Deliver the small project and present findings.
  - Shadow main workflows (deploys, triage, design reviews).
  - Complete two cross-functional introductions.
- Manager deliverables: weekly 1:1s, feedback at 30-day checkpoint.

Day 61–120: impact & career conversation
- Objectives:
  - Lead a medium-scope project or feature.
  - Demonstrate independent execution and cross-team coordination.
  - Prepare a 90–120 day review packet: accomplishments, blockers, and development goals.
- Manager deliverables: 90 and 120-day review conversations; align on success metrics and development plan.

90/120-day evaluation rubric (manager uses to guide conversation)
- Signals of success (examples): delivered assigned scope, communicative and responsive, adopted team practices, positive peer feedback.
- Areas requiring attention: needs additional mentorship, performance gaps, cultural/behavioral concerns.

Performance & feedback cycles integration
- New hires are added to the standard performance cadence after their 90-day checkpoint. For levels with probationary reviews, managers must document progress and escalate to people-ops if risk of separation is >30% at day 90.
- Feedback cadence: 1:1 weekly for first 90 days, then standard 1:1 cadence per team. People-ops recommends documented 1:1 notes stored in manager wiki.

Onboarding success metrics (people-ops will track quarterly)
- Time to first PR/merge (goal: <= 30 days for engineering ICs).
- Time to independent ownership of a component (goal: <= 90 days).
- New-hire onboarding NPS (survey at day 14 and day 90; target NPS >= +40).

Escalation and separation guidance
- If a new-hire shows sustained performance issues between day 30–90, manager must: 1) document examples, 2) run an improvement plan with clear milestones (30 days), 3) loop in people-ops for coaching.
- People-ops will provide legal/termination checklist if separation proceeds.

Manager quick-start guide (5-minute read)
- Before offer: write a crisp success profile (3 success metrics).
- Before day 1: assign buddy, create 30/60/90 outcomes, reserve 1 hour for architecture deep dive.
- Weekly: document one piece of feedback, schedule a short peer sync for cross-team visibility.

Templates and examples
- Interview scheduling email (short):
  "Hi {candidate}, thanks for applying. We’d like to schedule a 45‑minute interview to go over your experience and a technical exercise. Are you available: [times]?"
- 30-day checkpoint template (manager -> people-ops):
  "New hire: {name}, start: {date}, status: on-track/at-risk, notes: {summary}"

Sample JSON snippet: interview feedback (to paste into the interview form)
```
{
  "candidate": "Jane Doe",
  "role": "Software Engineer",
  "interviewer": "Alex Chen",
  "scores": {"problem_solving": 4, "system_design": 3, "collaboration": 5},
  "recommendation": "hire_with_feedback",
  "notes": "Strong collaborator; needs deeper system design examples."
}
```
Related documents & links
- Offer approval and comp bands (related_pages)
- IT & security new-hire checklist (related_pages)

Maintenance and governance
- Owner: people-ops (Aisha Patel). Review cadence: annual review in Q4 + immediate updates for legal or significant process changes.
- Change process: propose changes in PR to this doc, run pilot for one quarter, then update handbook after calibration session.

Appendix: common scenarios (fast answers)
- Remote hires across APAC: set start times that accommodate overlap with US teams; ensure payroll and benefits check with finance.
- Hires requiring visa sponsorship: escalate at role kickoff; expect 60+ day timeline and variable costs.
- Re-hiring ex-employees: follow rehiring policy and cooling period (see policies doc).

End of handbook. For questions or to request templates, contact people-ops@redwood.com.
